title: CCNA vs CompTIA Network+: Which First in 2026?
subtitle: Which networking cert to start with in 2026

pros: The #1 recognized credential in networking — big carriers, IT services firms, banks.
A technically deep exam (routing, switching, security, automation).
Senior median salary of €55k in France (APEC 2026).
Prepares you for the CCNP — a real Cisco career path afterward.
cons: $300 for the exam, ~200 hours of study — a heavy investment.
Very Cisco IOS/NX-OS oriented — less universal than people claim.
Includes labs/simulations — not just multiple choice.
certs.bestFor: You want a real networking career (NOC, network engineer, ISP, carrier).

pros: Vendor-neutral — concepts that carry over to Cisco / Juniper / Arista / Aruba.
A more predictable exam — mostly multiple choice.
Recognized for US government / DoD work (8570/8140 baseline).
An excellent prelude to the CCNA — you learn the concepts before the Cisco syntax.
cons: Limited recognition outside the US and the defense sector.
$369 — paradoxically more expensive than the CCNA.
Won't carry you to a senior networking career on its own — you'll need to follow up with the CCNA/CCNP.
certs.bestFor: You're new to networking and want to test your interest before investing 200 hours in the CCNA.

verdicts.profile: You already know you want to work in networking for the next 5 years.
verdicts.why: The CCNA's career ROI crushes Network+. Employer recognition is unambiguous.

verdicts.profile: You're not sure networking is for you — you want to test it.
verdicts.why: A lighter investment (~120 hours vs 200), and a less intimidating exam. If you enjoy it, move on to the CCNA.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting a DoD / US contractor role.
verdicts.why: Network+ is a DoD 8570/8140 baseline — the key to many US security contracts.

verdicts.profile: You want the best salary from year one.
verdicts.why: Junior median salary of €38k in France with the CCNA vs €33-35k with Network+ (Hays 2026).

tldr: CCNA if you know networking is your career. Network+ if you want to test the waters before committing 200 hours.
